THE_ANSWER_TO_THE_LICENCE_QUESTION: EXACTLY ONE candidate in the library is both suitable and licence-clear: Crimson Text. Every other suitable face is UNDETERMINED. If the owner wants Garamond/Caslon/Minion, the cheap early cost is: activate via Adobe Fonts under a current CC subscription (possibly already held with Illustrator 2026), or buy a desktop licence. Caught now rather than after artwork is built on an unlicensed face.
dip0_reconciliation: dip0 recorded license_status UNVERIFIED for all of these ('no licence file in scope') — its scanner looked for licence FILES only and never read embedded name-table licence metadata. This census's embedded-metadata reads are finer-grained and supersede dip0's UNVERIFIED for the files named here; dip0's records are not edited.

LICENCE_PREDICATE_STATED_2026_08_14.which_fields_count: nameID13 (License Description) and nameID14 (License Info URL), read from the name table; plus fsType from OS/2; plus any licence FILE travelling with the font (none exist in materials/Fonts)
LICENCE_PREDICATE_STATED_2026_08_14.sufficiency: EITHER name field alone suffices for LICENCE-CLEAR when it AFFIRMATIVELY declares a known open licence — Crimson Text Regular is clear on nameID14 alone (scripts.sil.org/OFL, no nameID13); Merriweather Bold is clear on nameID13 alone (verbatim OFL 1.1 text with the SIL URL embedded). A field that merely points at a foundry legal page (adobe.com/type/legal.html) is NOT affirmative and yields UNDETERMINED.

An affirmative verbatim declaration governs over an external URL this repository cannot resolve — Merriweather's nameID14 (sorkintype.com/eula.html) is recorded as a disagreement, not resolved.
